prompt: Some people think it is harmful for people to watch advertisements, others think it improves our lives. Discuss both views and give your own.
essay:
Advertising has become an integral part of modern society and influences people in many aspects of their daily lives. While some people believe that advertisements have a detrimental impact on individuals by encouraging unnecessary consumption and materialistic behaviour, others argue that they provide useful information and improve people's quality of life. Although both viewpoints have their own merits, I believe that the advantages of advertising outweigh its disadvantages when it is properly regulated. This essay will discuss both perspectives before explaining the reasons behind my opinion.

Those who oppose advertising argue that it manipulates consumers and promotes excessive consumerism. For example, many companies use celebrities, emotional appeals, and glamorous lifestyles to persuade people to purchase luxury products that they do not actually need. As a result, consumers often make impulsive purchasing decisions and begin to associate expensive brands with success, happiness, and social status. Therefore, excessive exposure to advertisements can encourage materialistic values and place unnecessary financial pressure on individuals.

On the other hand, supporters believe that advertising plays a vital role in informing consumers and supporting economic growth. For instance, advertisements introduce new products, allow customers to compare prices and features, and help small businesses reach a wider audience. Moreover, the advertising industry creates numerous employment opportunities and encourages healthy competition, which ultimately benefits both businesses and consumers. Consequently, advertising enhances consumer awareness while contributing significantly to the overall economy.

In conclusion, advertisements can both negatively influence consumer behaviour and provide substantial benefits to society. Nevertheless, I believe that their positive contributions outweigh the drawbacks, provided that governments impose strict regulations on misleading and harmful advertisements. If appropriate policies continue to be enforced, advertising will remain a valuable tool for promoting economic development while safeguarding consumers' interests.
